meta.title: tududi: self-hosted task manager and life management system, with MCP for AI agents
meta.description: A self-hosted task manager and life management system. Areas, goals, projects and tasks, plus notes and habits, with an MCP server exposing {{tools}} tools so AI agents can work your list. Open source under MIT.

ai.titleLine2: your AI agent can actually use
ai.ledeHtml: tududi ships an MCP server exposing {{tools}} tools, covering tasks, projects, areas, goals, habits, notes, people, tags, views, inbox, search and metrics. Connect Claude or any MCP-compatible agent straight to your system. Because tududi runs on your own server, the connection, and your data, never has to leave it. That's a structural difference Todoist and Notion can't offer, no matter what they promise.

habits.body: Track recurring habits alongside tasks and projects, with simple streaks and completion history.

recurring.title: Smart Recurring Tasks
recurring.body: Daily, weekly, monthly patterns with completion-based recurrence and parent-child relationships.

richTasks.title: Rich Task Organization
richTasks.body: Priorities, due dates, tags, and smart sorting. Powerful filtering to find what matters.

subtasks.title: Subtasks & Breakdown
subtasks.body: Break down complex tasks into manageable subtasks with progress tracking.

notes.title: Project Documentation
notes.body: Rich text notes for projects with full search and organization capabilities.

tags.title: Flexible Tagging System
tags.body: Custom tags for tasks and notes with instant filtering and cross-project organization.

search.title: Smart Filtering & Search
search.body: Full-text search plus filters by project, tag, priority, or due date. Find any task in seconds.

pwa.title: Install as an App
pwa.body: Add tududi to your home screen or desktop as a PWA. Works offline and syncs when you're back online.

oidc.title: OIDC / SSO Login
oidc.body: Sign in with your existing identity provider: Authentik, Keycloak, Google Workspace, or any OIDC-compatible provider.

i18n.title: Multi-Language Support

telegram.title: Telegram Integration
telegram.body: Send a message to capture tasks instantly, get daily digests, and manage your list on the go.

caldav.title: CalDAV Sync
caldav.body: Bidirectional task sync with Apple Reminders, tasks.org, Thunderbird, and any CalDAV-compatible app.

api.title: API Access & Swagger
api.body: Versioned Swagger docs and personal access tokens for custom integrations.

responsive.title: Responsive Design
responsive.body: A layout that adapts cleanly from a widescreen desktop down to a phone in your pocket.

faq.title: Questions worth answering before you commit
faq.sub: The licence, the AI, and what happens to your data. If something is missing, ask in Discord.

licence.a: tududi is open source under the MIT licence. You can run it, modify it, and build on it without paying anyone. There are no seat counts, no usage limits, and no features held back for a paid tier: the self-hosted version is the whole product. The paid options on this page sell hosting and support, not access.

commercialUse.q: Can I use tududi at work, or in my company?
commercialUse.a: Yes, and you do not need to buy anything first. The MIT licence permits commercial use, including inside a business and inside a commercial product, with no revenue threshold and nothing to report. If your organisation needs a support commitment or an invoice for its procurement process, that is what the Business Licence is for. It buys priority support, a response commitment, and paperwork, not permission.

maintained.a: Yes. It is built primarily by one maintainer, with contributions from the community, and it ships often. Every release is listed on the GitHub releases page, linked from the Changelog in the menu above, so you can judge the pace yourself rather than take our word for it. Development happens in the open: issues, a public roadmap, and a Discord where questions get answered.

shutdown.q: What happens to my data if tududi goes away?
shutdown.a: The app is MIT licensed and the source is public, so it cannot be withdrawn from you. Anyone can keep running it, and you can fork it. For Managed instances, your data lives in a standard tududi database that is not in a proprietary format; if the Managed service ever shut down, you would get your data and a guide to moving it onto your own server.

requirements.q: What do I need to run it myself?
requirements.a: Docker and somewhere to run it. You pull the image, run the container, and mount a directory for the database. It is comfortable on a small VPS or a machine on your own network, and the exact commands are in the Self-Host section above and in the docs.

dataLocation.q: Where is my data, and how do I back it up?
dataLocation.a: Everything lives in a single SQLite database file inside the volume you mounted. Backing it up is copying that file somewhere safe, and restoring it is copying it back. tududi also snapshots the database automatically before it applies migrations, keeping recent copies. There is no proprietary format and no export step standing between you and your own data.

multiUser.q: Can several people share one instance?
multiUser.a: Yes. A single instance can host multiple users, and projects can be shared with read-only or read-write access, which the tasks and notes inside them inherit. Self-registration is off by default, so an admin either creates accounts or deliberately opens sign-ups. Nobody gets in because you forgot to close a door.

mobile.a: tududi installs as a PWA rather than a native app. Add it to your home screen on Android or iOS, or install it on a desktop, and it behaves like an app: it reads from cache when you are offline and syncs your changes when you reconnect. There is nothing to download from the App Store or Play Store.

reverseProxy.q: Does it work behind a reverse proxy?
reverseProxy.a: Yes, and that is the normal way to run it. Set TUDUDI_TRUST_PROXY so the app trusts the forwarded headers from nginx, Caddy, or Traefik. If you skip it, logins and IP logging behave strangely in ways that are hard to diagnose, so the app raises a specific error rather than failing quietly. The accepted values are documented in the README.

aiOptional.q: Do I have to use the AI features?
aiOptional.a: No. Both AI layers are off until you switch them on, and tududi is a complete system without either. If you never enable them, nothing is missing and nothing nags you.

aiPrivacy.q: Does my data get sent to an AI company?
aiPrivacy.a: That depends which of the two layers you mean, and the difference matters. The MCP server runs inside your own instance: an agent such as Claude Desktop connects to your server, so the connection and your data stay where you put them. The AI Assistant is different. It calls an OpenAI-compatible provider, so if you point it at a hosted one, the contents of those requests go to that provider. Point it at a local model instead, such as Ollama or LM Studio, and nothing leaves your machine. It stays off until you supply a key, so this is always your choice rather than a default.

mcp.q: What is MCP, and what can an agent actually do?
mcp.a: MCP is the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting AI agents to real systems. tududi ships an MCP server exposing {{tools}} tools spanning tasks, projects, areas, goals, habits, notes, people, tags, views, inbox, search and metrics, so an agent can capture, find, update and finish work rather than just talk about it. It is opt-in, and it works with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, or any other MCP client.

whyManaged.q: Why pay for Pro when self-hosting is free?
whyManaged.a: You are paying to not run it. tududi Cloud gives you the same system with updates and backups handled for you, and Pro adds the AI Assistant, MCP, CalDAV sync, the Telegram bot and unlimited items. If you already run Docker and a reverse proxy, self-hosting is genuinely the better deal and we would rather you did that. Cloud exists for people who want the system without becoming its sysadmin.

freePlan.q: What does the free Cloud plan include?
freePlan.a: Up to {{freeTasks}} active tasks, {{freeProjects}} projects, {{freeNotes}} notes and {{freeStorageMb}} MB of attachments, with no time limit. Completed tasks do not count. If you reach a limit you keep everything and can still read, edit, complete and delete; only adding more waits until you are back under the limit or upgrade to Pro.

leaving.q: Can I leave, and what happens to my data?
leaving.a: Yes, at any time. Export everything as a single file from your profile and import it into a self-hosted tududi, which reads the same format. Deleting your account removes your data, attachments and backups from our servers and cancels any subscription.
